stories.headline: Anthropic to Brief Financial Stability Board on Mythos Vulnerabilities Found in Global Finance

key_facts.fact: Anthropic agreed to brief members of the Financial Stability Board on cybersecurity vulnerabilities its Mythos model has been identifying in the global financial system, at the request of FSB chair and Bank of England governor Andrew Bailey.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic is preparing to brief the Financial Stability Board on the cybersecurity vulnerabilities its Mythos model has been identifying in the global financial system, the Financial Times reported on Monday, citing people familiar with the plan. The briefing has been requested by Andrew Bailey, the Bank of England governor and FSB chair, and will be delivered to G20 finance ministries and central banks under the board's umbrella.

key_facts.fact: When directed to develop working exploits in internal testing, Mythos reportedly succeeded on the first attempt in more than 83% of cases.
key_facts.excerpt: When directed to develop working exploits against those flaws in internal testing, the model reportedly succeeded on the first attempt in more than 83% of cases. The dual-use implications were obvious to regulators before the model went on the road.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic has not publicly released Mythos and is currently running it under 'Project Glasswing,' a controlled-access programme limiting who can run the model and against what targets.
key_facts.excerpt: Mythos is currently being made [available] under 'Project Glasswing', the controlled-access programme Anthropic has set up to limit who can run the model and against what.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic describes Mythos as a cybersecurity model and has claimed it has found thousands of high-severity flaws across major operating systems and browsers.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic describes it as a cybersecurity model designed to surface long-standing vulnerabilities in browsers, infrastructure, and software, and has claimed it has already found thousands of high-severity flaws across major operating systems and browsers.

stories.headline: Bannon and 60+ MAGA Allies Urge Trump to Mandate Government Testing of Frontier AI

key_facts.fact: A group of more than 60 Trump allies — including Steve Bannon, Amy Kremer and Brendan Steinhauser — signed a letter organized by Humans First urging Trump to require mandatory testing and government approval of powerful AI systems before release.
key_facts.excerpt: A group of more than 60 loyal allies of President Trump is urging him to test and approve the most powerful AI models before they're released, according to a new letter shared first with Axios. The letter — signed by Steve Bannon and conservative anti-AI activists Amy Kremer and Brendan Steinhauser — puts a vocal faction of the MAGA base at odds with the White House's hands-off approach to AI.

key_facts.fact: The letter compares frontier AI to nuclear systems and aviation, citing potential to assist in designing bioweapons, breaking into critical infrastructure, or manipulating financial markets.
key_facts.excerpt: 'The most powerful AI systems, which can now, or soon will be able to, assist in designing bioweapons, breaking into critical infrastructure, or manipulating financial markets, should be treated with the same seriousness and care.'

key_facts.fact: Bannon told Axios the letter 'takes us next level' and 'lays out [that] we must have mandatory testing and government approval.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'This letter takes us next level,' Bannon tells Axios. 'The letter lays out [that] we must have mandatory testing and government approval.'

key_facts.fact: Humans First's tagline is 'technology should serve humans … not replace them,' and the letter supports policies requiring mandatory testing, evaluation, vetting, and government approval of potentially dangerous frontier AI systems before deployment.
key_facts.excerpt: 'For this reason, we support proposed policies that require mandatory testing, evaluation, vetting, and government approval of potentially dangerous frontier AI systems before they are deployed.'

sources.title: Scoop: 60+ MAGA allies tell Trump to vet AI before release

stories.headline: Torvalds Says AI Bug Hunters Made Linux Security Mailing List 'Almost Entirely Unmanageable'

key_facts.fact: In his Linux 7.1-rc4 release post on May 17, Linus Torvalds wrote that 'the continued flood of AI reports has basically made the security list almost entirely unmanageable, with enormous duplication due to different people finding the same things with the same tools.'
key_facts.excerpt: Some of the documentation updates might be worth highlighting: the continued flood of AI reports has basically made the security list almost entirely unmanageable, with enormous duplication due to different people finding the same things with the same tools. People spend all their time just forwarding things to the right people or saying 'that was already fixed a week/month ago' and pointing to the public discussion.

key_facts.fact: Torvalds said AI-detected bugs 'are pretty much by definition not secret' and that treating them on a private security list is 'a waste of time for everybody involved,' since the reporters can't see each other's duplicate reports.
key_facts.excerpt: Which is all entirely pointless churn, and we're making it clear that AI detected bugs are pretty much by definition not secret, and treating them on some private list is a waste of time for everybody involved - and only makes that duplication worse because the reporters can't even see each other's reports.

key_facts.fact: Torvalds wrote 'AI tools are great, but only if they actually help, rather than cause unnecessary pain and pointless make-believe work,' and urged researchers to add value by reading the docs and creating a patch on top of what the AI did.
key_facts.excerpt: 'AI tools are great, but only if they actually help, rather than cause unnecessary pain and pointless make-believe work,' he wrote. 'Feel free to use them, but use them in a way that is productive and makes for a better experience.'

key_facts.fact: The kernel project added new documentation requiring AI-assisted bug reports to follow concise human-style formatting, stick to verifiable impact (no speculative theoretical consequences), and have the tool propose and test a fix before submission.
key_facts.excerpt: Many AI-generated reports lack an understanding of the kernel's threat model and go to great lengths inventing theoretical consequences. This adds noise and complicates triage. Please stick to verifiable facts (e.g., 'this bug permits any user to gain CAP_NET_ADMIN') without enumerating speculative implications. Have your tool read this documentation as part of the evaluation process.

sources.title: Linus Torvalds says AI-powered bug hunters have made Linux security mailing list 'almost entirely unmanageable'

stories.headline: Baidu Q1 Tops Estimates as Core AI Revenue Jumps 49%, Cloud Infra Up 79%

key_facts.fact: Baidu reported Q1 2026 revenue of 32.08 billion yuan, ahead of the 31.49 billion yuan consensus estimate, with adjusted profit of 12.06 yuan per ADR vs 11.84 yuan forecast.
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue came in at 32.08 billion yuan, ahead of the 31.49 billion yuan consensus estimate. Adjusted profit per American depositary receipt of 12.06 yuan edged past the 11.84 yuan forecast.

key_facts.fact: Baidu Core AI-powered business revenue rose 49% year over year to 13.6 billion yuan and exceeded half of Baidu General Business revenue for the first time.
key_facts.excerpt: Baidu Core AI-powered business generated revenue of 13.6 billion yuan, up 49% year-over-year, while the broader Baidu General Business contributed 26 billion yuan in revenue, with adjusted operating profit of 3.95 billion yuan. 'In Q1, our Core AI-powered Business exceeded half of Baidu General Business revenue for the first time, marking a clear signal that AI has become the core driver of Baidu,' said CEO Robin Li in a statement.

key_facts.fact: Cloud infrastructure revenue surged 79% year-on-year to 8.8 billion yuan in Q1, with GPU cloud revenue more than tripling, up 184%.
key_facts.excerpt: Baidu said its cloud infrastructure revenue surged 79% year-on-year to 8.8 billion yuan in the first quarter, with GPU cloud revenue more than tripling, up 184%. AI applications revenue was broadly flat at 2.5 billion yuan.

key_facts.fact: Apollo Go delivered 3.2 million driverless rides in the quarter, with triple-digit growth in fully-driverless rides as the robotaxi unit expanded internationally.
key_facts.excerpt: The company delivered 3.2 million driverless rides last quarter, a significant increase from the previous year. The Core AI-powered Business, which accounted for half of Baidu General Business revenue, exceeded half of the company's total revenue year over year. Meanwhile, Apollo Go saw triple-digit growth in fully-driverless rides, while advancing its international expansion.

sources.title: Baidu tops Q1 estimates as core AI-driven revenue surges 49%; shares up

stories.headline: Apple's Revamped Siri to Ship as Beta with Auto-Deleting Chats, Gurman Reports

key_facts.fact: Apple's new standalone Siri app in iOS 27 will include privacy features unique to the chatbot market and may launch as a beta test even after a two-year delay, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple's Siri app in iOS 27 will include privacy features unique to the chatbot market. Also: The new digital assistant may launch as a beta test even after being delayed for two years, and the company is planning a Genmoji upgrade in its new operating system.

key_facts.fact: The new Siri will include an auto-deleting chats feature modeled on iMessage — users can choose to remove conversations after 30 days, one year, or keep them indefinitely.
key_facts.excerpt: Gurman said Siri could include a feature similar to the Messages app, allowing users to automatically delete conversations after 30 days or one year — or to keep them indefinitely.

key_facts.fact: The standalone Siri app is expected to be powered by Google Gemini and offer a ChatGPT-style chatbot experience with stricter limits on how long user information is used and stored.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple will reportedly launch the first standalone Siri app, powered by Google Gemini and offering users a chatbot experience reminiscent of ChatGPT. But compared to those other chatbots, the app is supposed to have more limitations on how long user information can be used and stored.

key_facts.fact: Internal iOS 27 test versions use a 'beta' label on the new Siri and include a toggle to leave the beta, suggesting Apple may keep the unfinished branding through public release this fall.
key_facts.excerpt: Test versions of iOS 27 within Apple use this label for the new Siri and include a toggle to leave the Siri beta. Given that we're only a month out from WWDC, there is a strong chance that this approach will be used in developer beta versions and even when iOS 27 ships this fall.

stories.headline: GitHub Makes GPT-5.3-Codex the New Base Model for Copilot Business and Enterprise

key_facts.fact: Effective May 17, 2026, GPT-5.3-Codex became the base model for all Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise organizations, replacing GPT-4.1.
key_facts.excerpt: As announced on March 18, 2026, GPT-5.3-Codex is now the base model for all Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise organizations, replacing GPT-4.1. The base model is used when your organization hasn't yet approved other models through its internal review process.

key_facts.fact: GPT-5.3-Codex is GitHub's first long-term support (LTS) model, in partnership with OpenAI, guaranteed to be available for 12 months from its launch.
key_facts.excerpt: GPT-5.3-Codex is also our first long-term support (LTS) model, in partnership with OpenAI. LTS models are guaranteed to be available for a full 12 months from the model's launch date, giving enterprises the stability they need for internal security and safety reviews.

key_facts.fact: GPT-5.3-Codex launched on February 5, 2026, and will remain available through February 4, 2027 for Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise users.
